# PrevNext

Links to the texts before and after this one, with their titles.

```tsx
import { PrevNext } from '@kafka/react'
```

## When to use it

- At the end of an article that belongs to a series or a sequence.

## When not to

- For "related articles": it is a sequence, not a recommendation.

## Examples

### Previous and next

Use real titles, not "Previous article".

```tsx
<PrevNext prev={{ href: '#anterior', title: 'La arquitectura del texto' }} next={{ href: '#siguiente', title: 'Umbrales de lo cotidiano' }} />
```

### First text of a series

With no previous text, the next one keeps its place on the right.

```tsx
<PrevNext label="Primer texto de la serie" next={{ href: '#siguiente', title: 'Umbrales de lo cotidiano' }} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prev` | `PrevNextLink` |  |  |
| `next` | `PrevNextLink` |  |  |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the navigation. Defaults to the localised "More to read". Give each one a different name if a page has more than one. |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **Landmark:** a `nav` with an accessible name; give each one a different name if a page has several.
- **Links:** real `<a href>` with `rel="prev"` and `rel="next"`; the whole card is the link, at least 44 px tall.
- **Arrows** are decorative; the direction is in text.

## Content

- Show the real title of the destination.
